exposure: education about postpartum depression during pregnancy or after childbirth
clinician screening practices for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (PMADs)
outcome: receipt of mental health services (counseling/therapy, support groups, or prescribed medication)
cohort: The study sample consisted of 110 Black women who self-reported experiencing PMAD symptoms or being recently diagnosed with a PMAD, and lived in Los Angeles County, California throughout the perinatal period.
finding: Black women who received education about postpartum depression during pregnancy or after childbirth had almost 5 times higher odds of receiving mental health treatment than those who had not.
cross-section timing: Data was collected covering experiences throughout the perinatal period, specifically during pregnancy and after childbirth.
